citeinfo.title: transects_50m - Digital Shoreline Analysis System Version 6.2.104 Transects
citeinfo.othercit: This metadata record is a template for data created using the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) Digital Shoreline Analysis System (DSAS) version 6.2 application. Basic process steps and attribute fields have been described but MANY REQUIRED FIELDS HAVE BEEN LEFT BLANK in order for the DSAS user to enter their specifications. Therefore, this metadata file is not FGDC-compliant as is. DSAS version 6 is a desktop application that loads geospatial files (geoJSON or shapefile) saved by a Geographic Information System. The DSAS software requires users to import a reference baseline and a set of shoreline positions. DSAS will then generate measurement transects and shoreline intersections which it will use to calculate rate-of-change statistics. In addition, DSAS provides uncertainties associated with rates of change. This metadata file accompanies a transect file of the same name that was created using the Digital Shoreline Analysis System version 6.2.

dataqual.logic: These data were generated using the USGS Digital Shoreline Analysis System (DSAS) version 6.2, an automated software program which does not perform checks for fidelity of the input features. Any testing on these data should be carried out by end-users to ensure fidelity of relationships.
dataqual.complete: This dataset contains transects generated by the USGS Digital Shoreline Analysis System (DSAS) version 6.2 application. Incomplete fields in the metadata record should be updated by the DSAS user.

procstep.procdesc: Transect features were generated using DSAS version 6.2.104 or were imported from a previously existing transect dataset and updated for use within DSAS version 6.2.104. Parameters Used: baseline layer=ligne_de_base_v2, baseline placement=onshore, Optional baseline parameters used=N, transect spacing=50, transect length=1000, smoothing value=500, shoreline layer =traits_de_cote_annuels. Transects clipped to shoreline extent N.

enttyp.enttypd: Transects were generated by DSAS at a 90 degree angle to the user-specified baseline using a user-specified smoothing algorithm to maintain roughly parallel transects that are orthogonal with respect to the baseline. Transects are returned witin a geoPackage, and can be exported from DSAS as .shp, .geoJSON, or .csv format based on user preference.

attrdomv.udom: Unique whole numbers that are automatically generated.

attr.attrdef: Unique identification number of the baseline segment. If BaselineID=0 no transects will be generated. Used by DSAS to determine transect ordering alongshore if multiple baseline segments exist.
attr.attrdefs: U.S. Geological Survey, Woods Hole Science Center

attr.attrdef: Assigned by DSAS based on ordering of transects along the baseline. Allows user to sort transect data sequentially alongshore from baseline start to baseline end.
attr.attrdefs: U.S. Geological Survey, Woods Hole Science Center

attr.attrdef: Assigned by DSAS to indicate whether or not a DSAS-generated transect has been modified (0= auto-generated DSAS transect; 1= DSAS transect has been edited by the user).
attr.attrdefs: U.S. Geological Survey, Woods Hole Science Center

attr.attrdef: Assigned by DSAS to to record the orientation of the transect as measured by DSAS. Prior to version 6.2, this field was called Azimuth. For DSAS v6.2, TransAngle (or transangle) is defined as the clockwise angle between the north vector and the vector of the transect (starting at the LANDWARD end and ending at the seaward end). Please note, this definition of TransAngle is different than the definition of Azimuth used in past versions of DSAS.
attr.attrdefs: U.S. Geological Survey, Woods Hole Science Center

attr.attrdef: Length of feature in internal meters.

attrdomv.udom: Positive real numbers that are automatically generated.

attr.attrdef: The total cumulative distance (TCD) measures the distance along the baseline in meters from the start of the baseline segment with an ID=1 to the end of the last baseline segment.

The angle between the transect and the shoreline in degress (+/-) away from an orthoganal (90 degree) intersection. Ideally, transects used to calculate shoreline change should intersect the shoreline at a right angle. As the angle moves farther from 90 degrees, the calculated rate of change become less reliable and may not accurately represent the true rate of change.

overview.eaover: The entity and attribute information provided here describe the attributes that are generated using the Digital Shoreline Analysis System version 6 software. In some cases, the attributes described in this metadata file may not exist in the dataset. It is up to the DSAS user to verify the attributes and ensure all values are populated with regard to their dataset. In some cases attribute names will be capitalized within DSAS, but the exported version will have the same attribute names in lowercase.
